name: Seventeen Moons Over the Shelf
description:
Released in 2191 on pirate-pressed vinyl and encrypted data chips, this compilation gathered seventeen artists from Tier 1 and Tier 2 who had never shared a stage — some who had never met in person. The project was coordinated through a mesh network node called the Seventeen Relay, organized anonymously in the aftermath of the Shelf Displacement Act, which rezoned three residential blocks in Tier 1 to make way for a Vantablack Media distribution hub. The album opens with a low drone of salvaged pipe resonance and never fully lets it go, threading that industrial breath through folk confessionals, polyrhythmic percussion workouts, and raw spoken-word cuts that name corporate officers by name.

Standout tracks include 'Relocation Notice,' a bitter ballad by Kindling Wren that layers West African call-and-response over Nordic drone strings — the song circulated so widely on pirate feeds that Vantablack's legal division issued three separate takedown orders, all ignored. 'The Weight of Being Counted' by an uncredited collective features quarter-tone brass over machine-stamped percussion and a chorus that became a chant at the 2192 Circuit labor marches. The closing track, 'Meridian Has No Memory,' runs eleven minutes and features no melody — only layered testimony from displaced residents over a single sustained chord.
creator: various
genre: protest folk, industrial drone, spoken word
audience: Tier 1 and Tier 2 residents, labor organizers, underground archivists, anti-corporate activists
cultural_impact: The album became the de facto soundtrack of the 2192 Circuit labor marches and is considered a foundational document of the post-Displacement Act resistance movement. Corporate censors flagged it within weeks of release, but physical copies passed hand to hand with such persistence that estimates suggest over forty thousand copies exist in various formats across the lower tiers. The Vantablack legal team's aggressive pursuit of distributors only amplified its reach — the crackdown became a story that spread the music further. It is studied in underground community schools as an example of decentralized cultural production.
story_hooks: A player character discovers a mint-condition vinyl copy hidden inside a wall during a demolition job — someone sealed it there deliberately, possibly as a message or a time capsule.
One of the uncredited artists on the compilation has resurfaced under a new name and corporate contract; someone wants to expose them, someone else wants to protect them.
A Vantablack Media investigator is quietly searching for the original Seventeen Relay node operator, and the trail leads to someone the party knows.
